transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-02-12
- Time: 4:00 PM PST
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE); Sam Carter (Meridian CTO), Aisha Khan (Lead Eng), Diego Morales (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick SDK integration walkthrough focusing on Python and TypeScript quickstarts, environment & auth (API key vs SSO), basic streaming example, and next steps for a short pilot. Customer wanted clarity on auth, private deployment options, and how to measure token/latency cost.

00:00 - Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate you taking the time. quick agenda — Priya will run through the SDK quickstarts in Python and TypeScript, show auth, env vars, a streaming demo, and then we’ll capture next steps.
00:14 - Sam Carter: Yeah thanks, we're mostly interested in the quickstart — Aisha is going to be hands on; Diego's here for the network part.
00:22 - Priya Desai: cool, I'll share my screen, lemme know if audio is low. so first off SDKs — we publish both python and js packages. python is pip install redwood-inference, node is npm i @redwood/inference, (sometimes transcript shows different package names) but the repo link is in the notes.
00:45 - Aisha Khan: okay so env and auth — how do we do keys and rotate, we're behind a bastion and use vault.
00:52 - Priya Desai: good q. we support simple API keys for hosted, and for enterprise/dedicated you can integrate with your KMS or HSM. recommended pattern is to store the REDWOOD_API_KEY in your secret manager and set it as an env var like REDWOOD_API_KEY locally or in your container. example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx. for vault it's a secret fetch on startup, same pattern. rotation is supported — you can revoke keys in the console.
01:20 - Diego Morales: and for VPC/private deployments, how does auth flow change? we need no egress to public internet ideally.
01:30 - Priya Desai: for Private (VPC/on-prem) you run a private control plane; auth can be mTLS within the VPC and you can connect to a local token service. you can also bring your own KMS, all audit logs stay in your environment. small note — sometimes my phonetic transcription says "private plane" instead of "private control plane".
01:48 - Jordan Lee: quick question on roles — do you need RBAC at token level? many customers want team-based keys.
01:53 - Sam Carter: yes we'd like RBAC and ability to scope keys per service.
01:57 - Priya Desai: yep we support scoped API keys, and Console provides a token-level view for usage and cost.
02:10 - Priya Desai: demo time — Python quickstart. I'm going to run a small snippet.
02:16 - Priya Desai: (typing) from redwood import RedwoodClient  # pseudo import, readme has exact api
02:24 - Priya Desai: client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
02:30 - Priya Desai: response = client.generate("Summarize the last quarter revenue by bullet points", model="redwood-3-small", max_tokens=200)
02:40 - Priya Desai: print(response.text) — that gives you the basic sync call. note: model name might be transcribed oddly here; our model catalog has curated names (redwood-3, rw-3-small, etc).
03:05 - Aisha Khan: what's the latency on that for ~150 token responses?
03:10 - Priya Desai: depends on plan — hosted single request is typically 100-300ms for base models under 512 tokens in our benchmarks, but more complex setups vary; if you need strict p95 latencies we recommend Dedicated with pinned capacity. we can share benchmark spreadsheets.
03:26 - Diego Morales: about batching and throughput — how do we handle high qps?
03:30 - Priya Desai: our runtime supports continuous batching, automatic prefix caching and kv-cache for chat. you control batching via client-side concurrency and the batching config in the deployment. for very high qps you can go dedicated and tune autoscaling.
03:45 - Priya Desai: switching to TypeScript quickstart — (typing) import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
03:52 - Priya Desai: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
04:00 - Priya Desai: // streaming example
04:03 - Priya Desai: const stream = client.stream.generate({ model: 'redwood-3', prompt: 'Write a short product blurb for a new retail checkout feature' })
04:10 - Priya Desai: stream.on('data', chunk => { process.stdout.write(chunk) })
04:14 - Sam Carter: nice, can we do function/tool calling? we have internal inventory service and want the model to call inventory API.
04:20 - Priya Desai: yes function calling is supported — you can register tool schemas and the runtime will emit structured json. small warning — the transcript may say "function calling is experimental" but we support it in hosted and Dedicated; for Private you may need to expose internal tools via secure connectors.
04:40 - Aisha Khan: what about cost measurement? we need token and cost visibility per team.
04:46 - Jordan Lee: Console has token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and you can export usage. Redwood Optimize suggests batching/quantization to reduce token spend. we'll share a sample CSV from Console.
05:05 - Diego Morales: security docs — do you have SOC2 and network diagrams?
05:10 - Jordan Lee: yes, we'll attach SOC2, ISO summary, and a network architecture diagram. Also our security pack includes SSO (SAML/OIDC), audit logs, and KMS integrations.
05:20 - Sam Carter: can we try a small pilot, maybe 2 weeks, test 3 endpoints, measure latency/cost?
05:26 - Jordan Lee: totally. typical pilot is 2-4 weeks. We do a smoke test, then a short benchmark (we can run with a 500 qps synthetic), and then a pilot contract for Dedicated if that's needed.
05:40 - Priya Desai: one more demo note — local dev quickstart: you can use the hosted sandbox key for dev (limited quota). for CI, put keys in secrets manager and rotate. sample repo includes docker-compose for local mocking.
06:00 - Aisha Khan: how does fallback work if a model is unavailable? we want graceful degradation.
06:06 - Priya Desai: smart routing and automatic fallback — we can route by latency/cost and fallback to a cheaper compatible variant. also can set up automatic A/B rollouts via Console.
06:18 - Sam Carter: ok are there any gotchas for TypeScript consumers?
06:22 - Priya Desai: watch for streaming backpressure; the examples show event handlers. also ensure your bundler includes the right polyfills if you run in older node. docs have a troubleshooting section.
06:35 - Diego Morales: networking specifics — we'll need an IP allowlist for our firewall, or VPC peering. is there an option for private endpoints?
06:42 - Jordan Lee: yes, Private supports VPC peering, private endpoints and on-prem deployments. Diego, we'll include a config doc with required ports and peering steps.
06:56 - Sam Carter: great. timeline — we'd like to run smoke tests next week and decide on pilot budget.
07:02 - Jordan Lee: noted. I'll follow up with pricing and pilot options.
